QF.id: Concept and Role of Mutual Fund_3

question.text: The face value of a mutual fund unit in India is typically:

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that every mutual fund unit typically has a face value of Rs. 10, and that units in a New Fund Offer (NFO) are sold to investors at the face value of Rs. 10 per unit. After the NFO, the price moves to NAV, which fluctuates with the market value of the underlying portfolio; face value remains the original reference unit capital figure. The Trap: The remaining options pick other amounts that do not reflect the standard mutual fund unit face value. Candidates who guess based on general market prices or unrelated instruments will choose them. Note: Source page 39 supports the typical Rs. 10 face value and unit capital, and page 170 supports NFO units being allotted at the Rs. 10 face value.
